catalog_quote: The following rules are concerned with the placement of accent in words. Such rules must account for the fact that a word will only have one accent mark in the terminal string (unless there is no inherent accent in any of the constituent forms). The placement of that accent is a function of the inherent accents and their relationship to each other and junctures. [pp. 47-48] ... Rule 24 ... Occasional single syllable forms may appear. Innate accent for all forms is on the penult. Hence a form with only one syllable is given by the dictionary in the form ´S. If such a form is given by the syntax directly following a # or // juncture, accent is progressive to the only syllable of the form. Examples: #´ʔaŋ-a# ⇒ #ʔáŋ-a# house-n; #cáwar-a//´ci-a# ⇒ #cáwar-a//cí-a# dog-n//nose-n [p. 48] ... Rule 26 ... Example: #o´ken# ⇒ #ó-ken# 3(3)-sleep. Rule 27 ... Post-positionals which occur with weak innate accent lose their accent if preceded in the word by another accented syllable. Example: #ʔáŋ-a-pɨ̀pe# ⇒ #ʔáŋ-a-pɨpe# house-n-in. Rule 28 ... The innate accent of a postpositional becomes the word accent if not preceded by an accented syllable elsewhere in the word. [p. 49] ... Rule 29 ... This is the rule for zeroing all remaining innate accents within a word but the last one. ... Examples: #o-ápo-póta# ⇒ #o-apo-póta# 3(3)/3(3)-do-will ... #ce-ráʔɨr-a//raŋ-a# 1-son's-n//house-n Rule 24 #ce-ráʔɨr-a//ráŋ-a# (no other change) [p. 50]

new_statements.quote: Occasional single syllable forms may appear. Innate accent for all forms is on the penult. Hence a form with only one syllable is given by the dictionary in the form ´S. If such a form is given by the syntax directly following a # or // juncture, accent is progressive to the only syllable of the form. [p. 48] ... This is the rule for zeroing all remaining innate accents within a word but the last one. [p. 50] ... There are two inherent kinds of accent. ` is weaker, disappearing in a word when preceded by a strong accent. ´ is strong inherent accent which is only zeroed in a word where it is followed by a strong accent, unless // juncture should come between them. Accent is phonetically an intensification of the signal in relation to surrounding syllables, plus a higher pitch, plus slight lengthening of the vowel and surrounding consonants. [p. 28]

If such a form is given by the syntax directly following a # or // juncture, accent is progressive to the only syllable of the form.'; p. 50 Rule 29 'This is the rule for zeroing all remaining innate accents within a word but the last one.'; p. 28 'There are…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Every lexical formative (verb stem, noun stem, adverb, verbal suffix, particle) carries an inherent accent on its penultimate syllable; a monosyllabic stem projects its accent onto the syllable immediately preceding it (e.g. a prefix: #o-ken# > #ó-ken#) or, word-initially, onto itself. Within the phonological word all inherent accents except the last one are deleted, so each word surfaces with a single primary accent: on the penult of the last accented formative, which in the cited examples is the penultimate syllable of the word (#o-apo-póta#, #o-apo-pam-tar-áme#, #ó-ken#, #ʔáŋ-a#). Harrison 1975 (p. 41, p. 120) gives the same rule in Portuguese: 'O acento cai na penúltima sílaba de todo tema nominal', 'Coloca-se este acento gráfico na penúltima sílaba, seja real ou imaginário'.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Harrison 1975 rule 18 (p. 120): postpositions/relators (relacionadores) carry a secondary accent (`) on their penult; it is deleted when a primary accent is present in the relational phrase and promoted to primary when it is the only accent (Harrison 1971 Rules 27-28, pp. 49-50: #ʔáŋ-a-pìpe# > #ʔáŋ-a-pipe#; #i-pìpe# > #i-pípe#). Phrase-level pitch/intonation are explicitly left undescribed (1975 §2.11, p. 15).
new_statements.exceptions: Some formatives have no inherent accent (D, past-tense words, other subjunctives, the nominal marker A per 1975 rule 18). In possessor//possessed noun sequences (// juncture) both nouns keep their accent (1971 Rule 24 note, p. 48). Weak-accented postpositions lose their accent after an accented syllable, so a word like ʔáŋ-a-pipe surfaces with accent on its first syllable rather than the word penult. Accent regresses to the final syllable of the preceding form across = and - junctures (Rules 25-26).
new_statements.domain_note: Describes slow-speech citation pronunciation of words (the paper's stated scope). The rule is stem-level penultimate accent computed morphologically, then reduced to one accent per phonological word (#..#), so the surface word accent is the penult of the last accent-bearing formative, not always the penult of the whole word. Sentence/phrase stress and intonation are not described.
new_statements.identity_note: Both Harrison works describe the Asurini of the Trocará post on the Tocantins (Tucuruí, Pará), i.e. toca1235 [asu], based on fieldwork 1962-69. Not the Xingu Asurini (asn, xing1240): Nicholson 1978 'Aspectos da língua assuriní', named in the earlier scan note, is tagged asn in hh.bib and should not be counted for this language.

new_statements.quote: Intensidade 1. A penúltima sílaba em geral é acentuada. masa 'cobra', sawara 'cachorro/onça', aha 'vai', opotan 'gosta de'. 2, A anti-penúltima sílaba é acentuada nos seguintes casos: a. Numa palavra que tenha o sufixo -awa (V. Lição 19.) ma'e apotawa 'trabalho', ipira - pyykawa 'rede de pescar' b. Quando o verbo estiver na forma do Indicativo II (V. Lição 11.) isywi 'desce', ipyhygi 'pega'. [p. 5] ... Duração enfática: Para fins enfáticos, prolonga-se a penúltima sílaba de uma locução. Quanto mais prolongada a sílaba, maior a ênfase. [p. 4]
new_statements.translation: Stress. 1. The penultimate syllable is in general stressed: masa 'snake', sawara 'dog/jaguar', aha 'goes', opotan 'likes'. 2. The antepenultimate syllable is stressed in the following cases: a. in a word that has the suffix -awa (see Lesson 19 [verb nominalizer 'place/instrument']): ma'e apotawa 'work', ipira-pyykawa 'fishing net'; b. when the verb is in the Indicative II form (see Lesson 11 [prefix i-/h- and suffix -i]): isywi 'goes down', ipyhygi 'takes'. ... Emphatic length: for emphasis the penultimate syllable of a phrase is lengthened; the longer the syllable, the greater the emphasis.

new_statements.relation_note: Catalog record (Harrison 1971, classification morphological): innate accent of every form is on the penult, with accent rules zeroing all but the last innate accent in the word; existing statement held by the project reads 'fixed: penultimate syllable'. Nicholson 1978 states the same penultimate default and adds two named morphological cases of antepenultimate stress (-awa nominalizations, Indicative II forms), which is compatible with Harrison's account of accent placement depending on the constituent morphemes. It also settles the variety: the book describes Tocantins (Trocará) Asurini, not Xingú Asuriní as hh.bib tags it.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the penultimate syllable as the general rule; it falls on the antepenult when the word carries the nominalizing suffix -awa or when a verb is in the Indicative II form (suffix -i), i.e. these two suffixes do not count for stress placement. Emphatic lengthening also targets the penultimate syllable of the phrase.
new_statements.exceptions: antepenultimate stress (a) in words with the nominalizer suffix -awa, (b) in Indicative II verb forms (i-/h-.. -i); vowel length is contrastive (pe 'para' vs pee 'caminho') and distinct from emphatic lengthening of the penult.
new_statements.identity_note: Tocantins Asurini (Asuriní do Trocará / Akwáwa-Asuriní): Notas 1, p. 56: 'falada por umas cem pessoas.. no Posto Indígena de Trocará, na margem esquerda do Rio Tocantins e a uns 15 quilômetros abaixo do município de Tucuruí'; data collected at Trocará in 1973, 1975, 1976, 1977 and in the Assurini village on the Rio Pacajá (Nov 1973-Jan 1974). Not Xingú Asuriní (Nicholson's separate 1982 'Breve estudo da língua Asurini do Xingu' treats that language).

sources.note: p. 28: two inherent accents (weak ` and strong ´); accent = intensity + higher pitch + slight lengthening. p. 48 Rule 24: 'Innate accent for all forms is on the penult'; monosyllabic forms get accent on the preceding syllable (or on themselves after # or //).
